svg.title: H06 / MARS ODYSSEY RIDGEWORK engineering mission profile
svg.desc: H06, MARS ODYSSEY RIDGEWORK. Original project: Variability of Martian Wrinkle Ridges. Session H: Planetary Science. Scientific question: Does the observed variation within individual ridges require changes in thrust/backthrust geometry, or can sampling, erosion, and surface layering explain it? Testable hypothesis: A model with spatially correlated fault geometry will predict withheld ridge segments better than independent profile fits, while some apparent classes will disappear after measurement uncertainty is included.. svg.text: No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Turn along-strike wrinkle-ridge variability in Solis and Lunae plana into a
test of competing fault architectures and mechanical layering. Preserve the
original topographic classification goal while coupling descriptive shapes
to physical forward models. Published tectonic studies show that multiple
structural elements can reproduce complex ridge profiles; the proposed
analysis therefore reports model families and nonuniqueness rather than
treating a cluster label as a uniquely identified subsurface fault.

TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
A model with spatially correlated fault geometry will predict withheld ridge
segments better than independent profile fits, while some apparent classes
will disappear after measurement uncertainty is included.

Elastic dislocation and kinematic trishear models are competing
approximations, not interchangeable descriptions of the same physics.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Surface shape alone rarely constrains deep detachment depth uniquely.
